title: WEIGHT_DECAY 0.2 -> 0.0
description: Set cautious Muon weight decay to zero, keeping MATRIX_LR=0.06 baseline and everything else unchanged, to test whether decay is net-helpful or net-harmful in a 5-minute budget where it's rarely proposed on the log.
reflection: val_bpb=1.016251 vs baseline 1.012413 -- clearly worse (+0.38%), so cautious weight decay at 0.2 is net-helpful even in this very short training window, not just a long-horizon regularizer. Given the WEIGHT_DECAY schedule already decays to 0 by end of training (get_weight_decay = WEIGHT_DECAY*(1-progress)), it acts more like a stabilizer early/mid-training rather than a late-training regularizer -- removing it entirely hurts. Don't try WEIGHT_DECAY=0 again; if anything, a follow-up could test increasing it (e.g. 0.3) rather than decreasing. This round also had 5/6 proposals converge on near-duplicate DEPTH=10 or DEPTH=6 experiments -- worth flagging to the group that slot allocation should diversify more once proposals are visible, since 3x identical seed=42 runs of the same config waste budget.
